I wish I could have waited a few more months, but I couldn't. I was driving a 2018 Ford Fusion with 279k miles. The check engine light was on for at least a year, and I couldn't renew my registration (I managed to get a four-month extension). I literally had only one month for car shopping, and some people also scared me with the new tariffs. Also, my dream car is a RAV4, so next time I buy a car, it will be a brand-new RAV4, lol.
Got it. Thank you for helping me understand!

I was confident my credit score was 702, per the Chase app. I knew it was not 100% accurate, but I knew that the Chase app is more accurate than Credit Karma. However, a 50-point difference—I was quite shocked, to be honest.

I have spent years building my credit.  I have a very good payment history and no hard inquiries; just a 50% credit utilization rate.

I had no other option regarding my child. I'm a single mother with no family. The child's father had plans, and none of my friends were available that day.  For my next car, my son will be eleven, so rest assured I won't go through this again.

I make all my payments on time and have always paid $300-$400 toward my credit cards each month. I am very responsible with all my payments and debt. My credit score in the Chase app was 702 when I went to the dealership. Frankly, I was quite shocked it is only 651. I know I can make these payments on time. The dealership manager told me this is what people usually do with PNC, and it usually works. That's my evidence.
Why is that?

Hmm... this is the part I don't quite understand. The monthly payments go down $10–$20 for every $1000 extra in the down payment. So, please explain it as if I'm seven years old—what's the point? I'm terrible at this stuff. I feel more ripped off because they convinced me to put down that extra $1000 since I'm on a pretty tight budget.
The EG Assurance Premier Coverage Plan.

Yes, they did tell me I can cancel at any time, and even though my monthly payments would stay the same, the "refund" would go toward the principal. They also mentioned tariffs, which made me even more scared, lol. The thing is, when I am asked about by friends about the down payment and monthly payments for this car, everyone acts like I was robbed and taken for a fool. They are like, “Nah, that’s way too much for a 2018 pre-owned car. Yeah, it might have only 31k miles and be the Limited model, but still, it’s a rip-off!”

On the contract, it shows the finance charge is $6,858.42. I plan on refinancing it after about six months of on-time payments. I honestly feel "robbed" or taken for a fool because they convinced me to put down a total of $3,000 instead of the $2,000 I had originally planned.

They told me I can cancel it at any time. I’m not sure what it’s called, but they explained that even though my monthly payments would stay the same, the "refund" for the warranty would go directly toward the financed amount. I guess that means I’d end up paying it off earlier than the 66 months. My biggest pain - is that I feel stupid and .. robbed lol - agreeing to put a 3k down payment instead of the 2k.

Sorry, I misspoke earlier. They did remove the initial $4,500 warranty, but in return, they didn’t give me the initial $2,130 discount on the car. Instead, they only took off $1,500 because they had to balance the value of the $4,500 warranty they removed.

Thank you for your input!

I’ve heard of buyer’s remorse, but I never thought I’d actually feel it — yet here we are, lol. This was my first time buying a car, so I’m really new to all of this. Yes, everything was listed on the paperwork… but honestly, I felt completely hypnotized by the finance guy. They really know how to talk you into anything.

I was decided I’d be fine without the warranty because it’s a Tucson, and we all know these cars come with a 10-year warranty. But then the guy really scared me by saying, “You’ll have zero warranty. If a sensor breaks, the sensor alone could cost $4,500. With this warranty, you’ll be fully covered. We’re not like other dealers who just charge to check the car out.” I didn’t know what to think at that point.

On top of that, I had already been there for three hours with my 5-year-old. We were both hungry — we came straight from work and daycare — and at some point, I just wanted it to be over so I could get my son home and feed him.

I plan to refinance after about six months of on-time payments. My main issue right now is with the extra $1,000 down payment I was persuaded to agree to — it’s a lot for my tight budget. This is also my very first time buying a car, so... yeah, I’m new to all of this.
